key_insight: Train LLM routers without any human-labeled examples by using synthetic queries and answers generated from high-level task descriptions; this allows accurate per-query skill estimation and expert-model selection even when real labeled data and request distributions are unknown.
problem_solved: How to build effective LLM routers when ground-truth labeled data is unavailable and user request distributions are heterogeneous or unknown.
method: Use generator LLMs to produce synthetic query–answer pairs from high-level task descriptions, forming a fully generated training set.
Train a router to estimate per-query skill/performance of candidate expert models using only the generated data (annotation-free skill estimation).
At inference, route each incoming query to the selected expert LLM based on the router's estimated skill, enabling annotation-free expert selection.
impact: Enables practical, scalable routing systems without costly human annotation, improving adaptability to varied and unseen user distributions and reducing the data bottleneck for multi-model deployment.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: high-level task descriptions → generator LLM → synthetic Q/A dataset → router training → router selects expert LLM at inference
Side-by-side bar chart: performance of annotation-free (RGD) router vs. supervised router across multiple tasks
Heatmap or Sankey showing per-task/expert routing patterns (which expert is chosen for which query types)
Icon set: 'no labels' badge, synthetic data generator, model-selection arrow, and calibration/score gauge
paper_title: Routing with Generated Data: Annotation-Free LLM Skill Estimation and Expert Selection
paper_authors: Tianyi Niu, Justin Chih-Yao Chen, Genta Indra Winata, Shi-Xiong Zhang, Supriyo Chakraborty
